text:
In crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs, the run-held branch (`_ if run.held`, which covers low disk, build-slot wait and budget short) writes `item <id> is left queued`. It does this even when the job was already dispatched and had spent on planning. Jobs 20261113-161230-49ph, -151949-mjpz and -112906-kjvt have planning records and no outcome. On 13 Nov the the person running Athena found them shown as interrupted and missing from `athena plan`. Fix this so the note is true: (1) a job held after dispatch must go back into the plan at its old priority, so the next drain resumes or retries it; or (2) if it cannot go back, the note must name the job's real state and the command that resumes it. Add a drain test with a low-disk hold after planning. The test must check that the item appears in `athena plan` afterwards, or that the note names the interrupted state. Add a CHANGELOG.md entry.

Acceptance:
- The change is made as described: When a job is held for low disk after it has started, the drain says it is 'left queued', but the job is marked interrupted and nothing runs it again
- No unrelated behavior changes; the existing tests pass
- fmt, clippy and test pass
